About Meridian

A long-term owner of essential businesses.

We don't buy companies to sell them. We buy good businesses, give them capital and patience, and help them become great.

Meridian began as a single freight company with eleven trucks. Today our four divisions serve more than 30,000 customers, from global retailers to local councils. Each company keeps its own name, leadership and culture, while sharing the group's financial strength, governance standards and purchasing power.

Our approach is simple: invest for decades, not quarters, treat people fairly and leave every community we work in better than we found it.

James WhitfieldGroup Chief Executive
Our businesses

Four divisions, one standard.

Each division is led by an experienced management team and reports to the group board, with clear targets for growth, safety and sustainability.

Meridian Logistics

Road freight, warehousing and last-mile delivery across Europe, with 140 distribution centres and 6,000 vehicles.

Visit Meridian Logistics

Meridian Energy

Developer and operator of solar and onshore wind farms, generating 2.1 GW of clean power for 1.4 million homes.

Visit Meridian Energy

Meridian Estates

Commercial and residential property, including 9,800 rental homes and 3.2 million sq ft of office and retail space.

Visit Meridian Estates

Meridian Industries

Precision components and electrical systems for automotive, rail and medical equipment makers in 14 countries.

Visit Meridian Industries
Our history

Thirty-nine years of steady growth.

1987

Eleven trucks

Robert Hale founds Hale Freight in Manchester.

1998

First acquisition

Purchase of Northgate Warehousing doubles the business.

2006

Meridian Group formed

A new holding structure brings property and industry under one roof.

2014

Listed in London

Shares admitted to the London Stock Exchange main market.

2023

Energy division

£1.1bn committed to renewable power by 2030.

Leadership

The team guiding the group.

James Whitfield

Group Chief Executive

Elena Marsh

Chief Financial Officer

David Kerr

Chair of the Board

Omar Siddiqui

Chief Operating Officer

Sustainability

Responsible growth, measured every year.

Our 2030 commitments are approved by the board and independently audited. Progress is published in full in our annual sustainability report.

64%

Lower carbon emissions

Scope 1 and 2 emissions cut since 2019, on track for net zero operations by 2035.

42%

Women in leadership

Of senior management roles across the group, up from 27% five years ago.

£18m

Community investment

Given to apprenticeships, local charities and skills programmes since 2020.

12 March 2026

Full-year results: revenue up 9% to £4.2bn

All four divisions grew, with energy and logistics leading. The board proposes a final dividend of 38.5p per share.

3 February 2026

Meridian Estates completes Leeds riverside scheme

412 new rental homes, a quarter of them affordable.

18 January 2026

1,000 apprenticeships by 2028

A new group-wide programme for school leavers and career changers.

Careers

Build a career across four industries.

From engineering and finance to operations and property, Meridian offers long-term careers, real responsibility and the chance to move between our companies as you grow.

The upstream/ folder preserves original source with its MIT notice. Root index.html is the separately documented MigBits adaptation.

Replace fictional sample business content, connect your own backend and retain the included license notices. Forms, data and payments are demonstrations.

Use Pause motion or your operating system reduced-motion preference. Full production and accessibility review remains your responsibility.

Original single-file HTML/CSS/inline JavaScript retained separately with creator MIT notice.

Stock photography, external fonts, favicons, metadata and remote services are excluded from the runnable edition; original HTML references are preserved as text only.

Original MigBits geometric demo artwork and motion controls are separate adaptations. Forms and checkout are frontend demonstrations, not backend services.

No React conversion is claimed. System font fallback changes the upstream typography. Render validation is not a complete accessibility audit.

Mobile grid minimum widths and word wrapping are corrected for community-center and nonprofit-charity. Dynamic photo references and initially empty image viewers use original artwork.

The original download-promotion toolbar is removed from runnable pages; creator attribution and complete copyright notices remain. Photo credit labels reflect the replacement MigBits artwork.
